discoveries.headline: A week of crypto law, from London to Hong Kong
discoveries.why: Lawyer Michael Handelsman's weekly round-up is a calm way to see where crypto rules are heading around the world. This week the UK Treasury made new cryptoasset regulations, Hong Kong gazetted its Virtual Asset Services amendment bill ahead of a first reading on 2 December, and the US SEC charged eight entities over fake crypto trading platforms said to have taken more than $37 million. Education, not advice.
discoveries.meta_credit: Bitcoin.com News · Law and Ledger, by Michael Handelsman for Kelman.Law

discoveries.headline: A chemistry professor runs for Serbia's presidency
discoveries.why: Serbia's student movement, which beat Aleksandar Vučić's party in October's parliamentary elections, has chosen organic chemist Radomir Saičić as its candidate for the presidential vote on 27 December. N1 traces his path from the University of Belgrade lab and the Serbian Academy of Sciences to the protests that followed the Novi Sad railway station tragedy. A short, clear profile of the man the students hope will finish what they started.

discoveries.headline: The whales are coming back to Patagonia
discoveries.why: Humpbacks are returning to Argentina's Beagle Channel, where locals have identified 208 individuals since 2013, and endangered sei whales are back in the San Jorge Gulf. Last season counted 3,410 southern right whales, 2,600 sei and 250 humpbacks, a recovery largely credited to the 1986 commercial whaling ban, though warming seas and new oil and gas plans now crowd their waters. Meet Shima, the humpback who has come back eight years in a row.
discoveries.meta_credit: Mongabay Latam · edited by Alexandra Popescu
discoveries.credit: Photos: Paula Faiferman/Siguiendo Ballenas, Sebastián Dirube, Diego Cabanas/Proyecto Cetáceos San Jorge and others

discoveries.headline: Richard Davidson: well-being can be trained
discoveries.why: Neuroscientist Richard Davidson, whose research was shaped by the Dalai Lama's request that he study Buddhist meditation, says well-being is something we can practise, like a kind of mental hygiene. He names four parts you can grow, awareness, connection, insight and purpose, and points to a study where two weeks of compassion meditation made people warmer and more generous. A gentle Sunday reminder that a calmer, happier mind is built a little each day.
discoveries.source: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
discoveries.meta_credit: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health · Karen Feldscher

discoveries.headline: Why do we swear?
discoveries.why: The Infinite Monkey Cage digs into the psychology and history of swearing with comedian Darren Harriott, Dr Emma Byrne and Dr Richard Stephens. They ask why people swear, what taboo words do for us, and even what chimpanzees signal when they break the rules. Forty-two funny, surprising minutes for a Sunday walk.
discoveries.meta_credit: The Infinite Monkey Cage · BBC Radio 4

discoveries.headline: Ninajirachi wins the 2026 NSW Music Prize
discoveries.why: ARIA Award-winning Ninajirachi has won the $80,000 NSW Music Prize for her debut album I Love My Computer. On the same night at the Museum of Contemporary Art, hip-hop group 3% took the NSW First Nations Music Prize and R&B and soul artist BOY SODA was named Breakthrough Artist of the Year. Three great reasons to put on some local music today.
discoveries.meta_credit: NSW Government · Minister for Music and the Night-time Economy, with Sound NSW

discoveries.headline: The sleep sweet spot for slower ageing
discoveries.why: A Columbia-led study of about half a million UK Biobank volunteers found that sleeping 6.4 to 7.8 hours a day was linked with the slowest ageing across 17 organ systems. Both fewer than six hours and more than eight were tied to faster ageing, though the researchers, led by Junhao Wen, note the study shows links, not cause and effect. A good nudge to protect your evening wind-down ritual. General information, not medical advice.
discoveries.meta_credit: Columbia University Irving Medical Center · study led by Junhao Wen, published in Nature

discoveries.headline: A gentle morning flow for beginners
discoveries.why: Former yoga instructor Ena Music shares a simple sequence for starting the day: neck rolls, cat-cow, child's pose, downward dog, low lunge, forward fold and chair pose. Give it 15 to 20 minutes and it becomes an easy morning ritual to wake up the body. Listen to your body, especially if the poses are new to you.

discoveries.headline: Build up to the perfect push-up
discoveries.why: Personal trainers Ashley Carter and Sergio Pedemonte explain how to do a push-up well, from hand position and a straight line through your body to breathing as you lower and rise. If a full push-up is too much today, start against a wall, on your knees or with your hands raised, and move on when you can do five slow reps for three to five sets. Check with your clinician before starting a new program.
